title: Cursor pagination for an API

requirements.text: The next-page cursor is opaque and encodes the last sort keys, not an offset
Walking every page returns each item exactly once, using a unique tie-breaker for repeated sort values
Cursors are integrity-protected and expire; tampered, expired or malformed cursors are rejected with a distinguishable error
The page size is validated and clamped to a server maximum
Responses signal whether more pages exist (null next cursor or a rel=next link) so clients stop correctly
The database query seeks by the cursor keys on an index (keyset), not OFFSET scanning
A cursor cannot be replayed against a different tenant, filter or sort to read data outside the original query

evidence.name: cursor is opaque base64url, encodes the last sort keys (not an offset) and is signed with the active key
stable under concurrent inserts and deletes between pages: no duplicates and no skips (memory source)
PGlite: inserts and deletes between pages produce no duplicates and no skips
tampered, malformed, expired and wrong-key cursors are rejected with distinguishable errors
limit is validated and clamped to the server maximum; default applies when absent
an empty or exactly-full final page ends correctly
SQL builder: parameterized keyset WHERE/ORDER BY/LIMIT, row comparison for uniform order, OR chain for mixed, no OFFSET
PGlite: schema applies; the newest walk seeks on the index (Index Cond on the cursor keys)
scope binding: a cursor reused by another tenant, with other filters or with another sort is rejected
PGlite: a cursor is bound to tenant and filters; filtered walks never leave the scope

implementations.notes: Cursors are signed, not encrypted; sort columns must be NOT NULL numbers or strings. PGlite tests run on one connection.
